\begin{lemma}[Possible outcomes of one abstract step]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.astep_cases}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.astep_cases}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.ValidPair, Complexity.LogProg.ValidPlain, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,d$ be natural numbers, let $\Lambda$ be a type, let $x$ be a finite bit string,
let $A$ assign to each control state an instruction with $m$ registers, $d$ oracle
indices, and states in $\Lambda$, and let $o$ be a Boolean oracle on indices in
$\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ and finite bit strings. For any control state $l$, register
assignment $v:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\mathbb N$, and stored answer
$res\in\{\mathrm{none},\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}$, one abstract step from
$(l,v,res)$ either yields an active configuration $(l',v',res)$ for some state $l'$ and
register assignment $v'$, or yields a halted configuration
$(\mathrm{none},v,\mathrm{some}(b))$ for some Boolean answer $b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Live result remains unset]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.astep_live_res}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.astep_live_res}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.astep_cases}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,d$ be natural numbers, let $\Lambda$ be a type, let $x$ be a bit string, and let
$A$ be an arithmetic register machine with an oracle assigning a Boolean answer to each
of its $d$ deciders on every bit string. If one step from a configuration with active
state $l$, register contents $v$, and unset result produces active state $l'$, register
contents $v'$, and result $r$, then $r$ is unset.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariant along a finite simulation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.inv_of_simTo}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.inv_of_simTo}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.SimTo, Complexity.LogProg.armProg, Complexity.LogProg.inv_of_mid, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let a register program, its initial label, an oracle, a decider machine, and a
starting-state assignment be fixed, together with natural numbers $B,W$ and
configurations $c,c'$ on the same Boolean input. If the program reaches $c'$ from $c$ in
finitely many steps and, at every step before the endpoint, no oracle-call state is
active and every register head position lies between $-1$ and $W$, then there is a
finite run length realizing this same endpoint such that the invariant holds at every
configuration before the endpoint.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Simulation of one register-program step]

\difficulty{6}
Let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers and access to $d$ Boolean oracles, and
let $D$ be a machine with $k_D$ work tapes and designated initial states $q_0(j)$.
Suppose one abstract step from the active configuration with control state $l$, register
values $v$, and no stored answer yields the active configuration with state $l'$, values
$v'$, and no stored answer. Suppose the starting configuration satisfies the
precondition for $A$, and for every register $r$ the bit length of $v(r)+1$ is at most
$W$. Then the compiled machine, started in the seam configuration encoding $l$, $v$, and
output word $out$, reaches the seam configuration encoding $l'$, $v'$, and the same
output word after some finite number $T$ of steps; at every earlier time $t<T$, its
configuration satisfies the stated invariant for $A$, $l_0$, $B$, and $W$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reachability simulation by the tape machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.arm_reach}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.arm_reach}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.Pre, Complexity.LogProg.armProg, Complexity.LogProg.arm_step, Complexity.LogProg.arun, Complexity.LogProg.arun_halted, Complexity.LogProg.arun_succ, Complexity.LogProg.aseam, Complexity.LogProg.astep_cases, Complexity.LogProg.rrun, Complexity.LogProg.rrun_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{5}
Fix a Boolean input $x$, an arithmetic register program $A$, its initial state $l_0$, an
oracle, a multi-tape machine $D$, a choice of initial state for $D$ for each oracle
index, and bounds $B,W\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose an $N$-step register computation from
state $l$ and valuation $v$, with no answer yet, ends in state $l'$, valuation $v'$, and
no answer. Assume that at every earlier step its configuration satisfies the
register-program precondition for $D$ and the chosen oracle, and each register value
plus one has binary length at most $W$. Then the tape machine compiled from $A$ can run
from the initial tape configuration encoding $x,l,v$ and the given output word to the
corresponding configuration encoding $x,l',v'$ with that output word unchanged, while
its invariant holds at every earlier step.
\end{theorem}
